clue.text: Forestall demand for capital punishment?

definitions.meaning: to forestall is to intercept or prevent something before it happens
a cry calling for a beheading, as the Queen of Hearts might shout

explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to block in advance; read as an order, the two words call for someone to be beheaded, the capital punishment of the surface.

clue.text: Love admitted by His Majesty King Edward, becoming Mrs Simpson's husband

indicators.note: something admitted by another is let inside it, so the letter for love goes within the abbreviation

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
ER, Edwardus Rex, is King Edward's royal cipher

explanation.surface: The abdication story: Edward VIII's love affair leading to his marrying the American Wallis Simpson.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Wallis Simpson, whose husband was Edward VIII himself; the Mrs Simpson meant is Marge of The Simpsons cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: In the cartoon The Simpsons, Marge is married to the bumbling father figure Homer.

clue.text: A fellow heard about Irish postal system

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the A and the sound-alike word wrap the abbreviation for Irish
heard tells us to take the spoken sound of the word for a fellow, spelt differently

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a man talking about the Irish postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is the service carrying letters by aeroplane, a system for sending post.

clue.text: Two daily newspapers follow Observer's lead quite regularly

indicators.note: the newspapers follow, coming after the opening letter in the answer
a word's lead is its opening letter, here of Observer's

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British daily
The Times is the other British daily paper

explanation.surface: A media note on how daily papers trail the Sunday Observer's lead story.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday paper; the FT (Financial Times) and The Times are dailies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofttimes is an old-fashioned word for frequently, meaning often or quite regularly.

clue.text: Welcomed in by padre, soldiers, say, come together

indicators.note: being welcomed in by someone puts the guests inside that host's word

parts.note: a padre is a priest, addressed as father
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: An army chaplain welcomes soldiers into a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To foregather is to assemble or meet, an old synonym for gathering together.

clue.text: Discusses education qualification rejected by a teachers' newspaper

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the qualification's letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree
the TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a newspaper for teachers

explanation.surface: A teachers' paper turns down an article on a teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Debates as a verb means argues over or talks through, the same as discusses.

clue.text: Quantity of medicine making one drowsier, if given regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word drowsier, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A warning that a medicine taken at regular intervals causes drowsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a measured amount of a drug taken at one time.

clue.text: Sort of telephone that's cooler

definitions.meaning: old British slang for the phone
a fan or device that blows air to cool something

explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls the telephone 'the blower', and a fan that blows air is a cooling device.

clue.text: Worker at university registered on a Japanese course

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
R is the abbreviation for registered, as in the ® mark

explanation.surface: A temporary worker at a university signs up for a Japanese language course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a class of study but is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is battered, deep-fried seafood or vegetables served as a dish in Japanese meals.

clue.text: Criminal hardens in court

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are behaving badly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hardened criminal stands in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In court' looks like a phrase; 'in' is part of the fodder, HARDENS and IN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanhedrin was the supreme council and tribunal of ancient Jerusalem, a judicial body.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader turned over American deserter

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the abbreviation for American is written backwards

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader hands a US deserter over to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution, murdered in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Marat was a radical figurehead in revolutionary France.

clue.text: Large tract of land near river in part of Ireland

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, meaning large
a common is an area of open land shared by a community

explanation.surface: A description of a big area of land by a river in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Roscommon is a county in the Irish province of Connacht.

clue.text: University town's literary events

definitions.meaning: Reading is an English university town, so this is the town's name with its possessive
events at which authors recite their work to an audience

explanation.definitionFit: Reading in Berkshire has a university, and authors give recitals of their work at public occasions.

clue.text: Decline money offered by churchgoers for rubbish service!

parts.note: to decline is to turn down, refuse
the collection is money gathered from a church congregation

explanation.surface: A sour remark about a church service where the worshippers refuse to give money.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the pun: 'rubbish service' sounds like a poor church service but means the bin men.
explanation.definitionFit: The council's bin round gathers household waste, a service dealing with garbage.

clue.text: Western seen from the stalls?

parts.note: stalls suggest the seats nearest the stage, but they are also where stabled animals stand, so this is a cowboy show as a stabled animal would see it

explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film or Western is jokingly called this, as its stars ride steeds.

clue.text: See 12
Winner, English ace raised … a glass of this?

parts.note: a champ is a champion, a winner

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: A is the ace in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A winning English tennis player who served an ace deserves a celebratory drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling wine from France is the drink poured by the glass to toast a victor.

clue.text: Duo producing tune on piano

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the tune follows the piano

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Two musicians perform a tune on the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something, the same as a duo.

clue.text: Deduce fashion company head has left base

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

indicators.note: the head of the word leaving means its first letter is removed

parts.note: Dior is a French fashion house

explanation.surface: Inference that a fashion house's boss has quit the company's base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like headquarters but is an adjective meaning low.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and inferior both describe something low in quality or worth.

clue.text: What researcher pens is mischievous

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the answer is held within the word researcher

explanation.surface: Asking what a scientist writes that is naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like writes but means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, playful manner, as in an arch smile, close to roguish.

clue.text: Force to abandon coal fire lit to provide some heat

indicators.note: lit, in the sense of drunk, suggests the remaining letters are jumbled
the abbreviation for force leaves the fodder, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Someone forced to give up their coal fire for warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a unit of heat energy, so one is a measured amount of warmth.

clue.text: Man to perform a Clapton medley at East London venue

indicators.note: at means next to, putting the abbreviation for East alongside

parts.note: Ken is a man's name
to sing is to perform music

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man performs a medley of Eric Clapton songs at an East London concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to east London, but East gives only the letter E; the anagram of A CLAPTON makes TONPALAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Kensington Palace is a royal residence in west London, a place to visit.

clue.text: Restrict road and rail transport either side of motorway

indicators.note: being either side of something means flanking it, so the motorway letter goes between the two pieces

parts.note: a tram is transport running on the road
the El is the elevated railway in American cities
M stands for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Proposals to limit road and rail traffic near a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hinder or hold back, so restrain or restrict.

clue.text: Goon from Greater Manchester area

definitions.meaning: a character in The Goon Show, the 1950s BBC radio comedy
a town west of Manchester, famous for its currant cakes

explanation.definitionFit: Eccles was a dim character on the BBC radio comedy The Goon Show, and also names a town near Salford.

clue.text: See 19
Group of hags almost completely against making contribution to charity

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

indicators.note: almost completely means nearly the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: A gang of old witches is almost entirely opposed to giving to charity.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a covenant is a formal pledge to pay a charity regular sums, often tax-efficiently.

clue.text: Fish barrel newly emptied

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

indicators.note: emptied means the inside letters of newly are removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A barrel of fish has just been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunny is another name for tuna, a sea fish.

clue.text: Spirit, say, or spirits

indicators.note: say means spoken out, so we take the sound of the drink

parts.note: gin is a spirit, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Debating whether to call a drink a spirit or spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'spirit' is the drink; the definition 'spirits' means supernatural beings of Arabian lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are supernatural beings of Islamic folklore, the plural of jinni, genies.

clue.text: Woman re-dealing after shuffle

indicators.note: after a shuffle, as with playing cards, the letters are in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman deals the cards again after shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraldine is a female first name.

clue.text: Late actor, popular fellow

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An obituary note for a well-liked actor.
explanation.walkthrough: John Inman was the British comedy actor of the sitcom Are You Being Served?, who died in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: John Inman was a well-known British comic performer, now dead.

clue.text: Writer, one erasing page about me

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened person wraps the word me
erasing means rubbing out, so the letter for page is removed from the person

parts.note: one means a person, as in 'one should'

explanation.surface: An author describes someone deleting a page about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist, an author.

clue.text: How speaker's words are received in a unionist meeting

parts.note: U stands for Unionist, as in Northern Ireland politics
a rally is a mass meeting

explanation.surface: A speech delivered at a gathering of trade unionists or Unionists.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken words reach the listener through the ears, by hearing.
